classification.difficultyReason: Connect sector arc length to cone circumference, then use Pythagoras to express the volume in one variable.

content.prompt:
A sector with angle $\theta$ radians is cut from a circle of radius 12 cm and formed into a cone by joining the straight edges so that the arc length becomes the circumference of the base.

Show that the volume $V$ of the cone is $$V=\frac{12\theta^2}{\pi}\sqrt{144-\frac{36\theta^2}{\pi^2}}.$$

spec.description: Major sector with downward-facing wedge removed, sector label, curved angle arrow labelled theta and radius labelled r; becomes separates it from a downward-pointing open cone with dotted interior seam, slant-length dimension r and red join arrow. Decorative pink face shading is omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: The sector radius and cone slant height are both 12 cm. The sector arc becomes the cone base circumference. The diagram's r denotes the slant length, not the base radius.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question diagram; no calculated dimensions or volume working supplied.

answer.worked:
Let $R$ be the cone's base radius and $h$ its perpendicular height, both in centimetres. The sector radius $r$ shown in the diagram is the cone's slant height, 12 cm.

The sector arc length equals the base circumference:
$$\begin{align*}2\pi R&=12\theta\\R&=\frac{6\theta}{\pi}.\end{align*}$$
By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=12^2-R^2\\h^2&=144-\frac{36\theta^2}{\pi^2}\\h&=\sqrt{144-\frac{36\theta^2}{\pi^2}}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac13\pi R^2h\\V&=\frac13\pi\left(\frac{6\theta}{\pi}\right)^2\sqrt{144-\frac{36\theta^2}{\pi^2}}\\V&=\frac{12\theta^2}{\pi}\sqrt{144-\frac{36\theta^2}{\pi^2}}\text{ cm}^3.\end{align*}$$
